activity_context.topic_title: Computing Partial Derivatives Using the Rules of Differentiation

feedback.problem: For the function $f(x,y,z)=x{z}^{3}-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y),$ evaluate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ at the point $(1,1,2).$
feedback.worked_solution:
We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the sum and constant multiple rules:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{z}^{3}-{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{z}^{3})-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)) \\  & ={z}^{3}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x)-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}) \\  & ={z}^{3}\cdot 1-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)\cdot 2x \\  & ={z}^{3}-2x\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi y)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we evaluate the partial derivative at the point $(1,1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}{|}_{(1,1,2)} & ={2}^{3}-2(1)\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi (1)) \\  & =8-2(1)(-1) \\  & =8+2 \\  & =10\end{aligned}
$$
